chapter: Tatum, Wiggins and Los Angeles friends
title: Wiggins's trio at the Turban Room and the start of Tatum's trio
summary: After Honolulu he played with Gerald Wiggins and Bill Douglass on Central Avenue until Tatum hired the bass and drums away.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: You mentioned Gerry Wiggins, and now I'd like to retrogress a bit. After I came back from Honolulu, I worked with Gerry Wiggins and Bill Douglass in a place called the Turban Room on Central Avenue.
That was downstairs in the Dunbar Hotel, was it not?
It was next door to the Dunbar Hotel. This is where Tatum used to come in all the time and listen to the group. And this gave Tatum the idea that he'd like to work with a bass and drums.
You mean he never had before that?

Well, he had worked with a bass and guitar, Slam Stewart and Tiny Grimes before. But for some reason, he gave that trio up and just did a single for a while. But then, when he heard our trio, he decided that he would like the same thing. So he hired Bill and I away from Gerry, and that was the start of a new Tatum trio. And we did many albums with that group, the albums with different people. Naturally, the Tatum albums, but we also recorded with Ben Webster, Buddy De Franco, Sweets Edison and maybe a few other people. But these Tatum albums are now, what, in the masterpiece series... They're in the hall of fame, that
group of albums that we did with Tatum. So whatever happens, I got in the Hall Of Fame.
That's the NARIS Hall of Fame?
Yeah, that's in the NARIS Hall of Fame. So I'm in there with Tatum, if with nobody else.
You're probably in there on some others, too.
